tasks.title: Implement template selection in tf_render_prompt based on engine field
tasks.accept: bash -c 'cd /home/[REDACTED]/git/agentflow && grep -q tf_select_template lib/dispatch.sh && grep -q content-worker lib/dispatch.sh && grep -q scenario-worker lib/dispatch.sh && grep -q scs-security-worker lib/dispatch.sh && grep -q CONTENT_TYPE lib/dispatch.sh && grep -q MIN_LINES lib/dispatch.sh && grep -q MIN_QUESTIONS lib/dispatch.sh && grep -q OUTPUT_FILE lib/dispatch.sh && grep -q MIN_CHALLENGES lib/dispatch.sh && grep -q EXAM_CODE lib/dispatch.sh && grep -q EXAM_SLUG lib/dispatch.sh && grep -q CATEGORY lib/dispatch.sh && echo All template selection features present'
tasks.acceptance_prose:
Modify lib/dispatch.sh to implement template selection in tf_render_prompt. Currently tf_render_prompt always reads prompts/worker.md regardless of task engine. It should select the template based on the engine field.

1. Add a tf_select_template function that returns the template filename based on engine:
   - engine content-deep-dive or content-practice-questions: content-worker.md
   - engine content-scenario-challenges: scenario-worker.md
   - engine security: scs-security-worker.md
   - engine content-* with vllm provider: content-worker-vllm.md (check provider via worker name parameter)
   - Everything else: worker.md (default)

2. Modify tf_render_prompt to accept an optional second parameter worker (worker name). Use it to look up the provider via tf_worker_field. If provider is vllm and engine starts with content-, use content-worker-vllm.md.

3. After selecting and loading the template, fill in ALL template-specific placeholders from the task config:
   - CONTENT_TYPE: from task .content_type field
   - EXAM_CODE: from task .exam_code field
   - EXAM_SLUG: from task .exam_slug field
   - MIN_LINES: from task .min_lines field
   - MIN_QUESTIONS: from task .min_questions field
   - OUTPUT_FILE: from task .output_file field (or from scope[0] if not set)
   - CATEGORY: from task .category field
   - MIN_CHALLENGES: from task .min_challenges field
   - CONTENT_TYPE_SECTION: for vllm template, a section based on content_type
   - TASK_DESCRIPTION: from task .acceptance_prose field (already done for worker.md, ensure it works for scs-security-worker.md too)

4. Update the tf_dispatch_one function to pass worker to tf_render_prompt: change tf_render_prompt $id to tf_render_prompt $id $worker

5. Ensure backward compatibility: if engine is empty or unknown, worker.md is used. If content-specific fields are missing, replace with empty string (do not leave unfilled placeholders).

6. The existing property test no_unfilled_placeholders must still pass: all mustache placeholders must be replaced.

7. Add at least 3 new property tests to tests/property/test-dispatch.sh:
   - Test that content-deep-dive engine selects content-worker.md (prompt contains content worker or certification)
   - Test that security engine selects scs-security-worker.md (prompt contains Security Task or infrastructure worker)
   - Test that content-scenario-challenges engine selects scenario-worker.md (prompt contains scenario or challenge)
   - Test that all placeholders are filled for content tasks (no unfilled placeholders)
   - Test that vllm provider with content engine selects content-worker-vllm.md
